messages:
nina: Quick RFC follow-up: propose we split the resolver into FastPath + HeavyEvaluator. FastPath decides a safe, deterministic candidate ordering for the sync hot path. HeavyEvaluator applies richer heuristics (latency model, cost curve, model-preference) and may run async or be rate-limited. Want feedback on contract.

omar: Sounds promising. Main Q: what does FastPath return? raw route ids or lightweight descriptors?

nina: Lightweight descriptors (CandidateHandle): {route_id, warm_score, static_cost_estimate, flags}. Small and copyable. FastPath returns ordered CandidateHandle[] plus a deterministic tie_seed.

kevin: Tie_seed is critical. Please ensure it's derived from tenant_id + request_id + cluster_seed so replicas resolve identically. No per-process RNG.

alice: How does HeavyEvaluator get invoked? sync in-path with a short timeout, or out-of-band?

nina: Both options supported: config flag per-policy. Default: try in-path with 20ms budget; if it returns in time, use its ordering. Otherwise use FastPath ordering and schedule an async evaluation to refresh cache for next requests.

david: If HeavyEvaluator is async and updates cache later, how do adapters observe that? We need a stable route id mapping surface so shims don't break.

nina: We'll expose a versioned decision token and per-route stable ids. Adapters will use route_id only. CandidateHandle.route_id is always present; the evaluator only changes ordering, not ids.

omar: Failure modes? If evaluator crashes or OOMs, don't degrade callers. Circuit-breaker + metrics needed.

kevin: Add circuit-breaker metrics: policy.evaluator.errors, policy.evaluator.timeouts, policy.evaluator.enabled (gauge). Also expose policy.decision.fallback_count.

alice: Auditability: we need reason codes on the chosen route for post-hoc analysis. Eg reason=FASTPATH_WARMTH or reason=EVAL_MODEL_PENALTY.

nina: Agreed. Decision record = {chosen_route, reason_code, decision_token}. We'll write strings for reason_code and a compact enum for agents.

david: Perf note: avoid heap allocations per candidate on hot path. Use small fixed-size arrays or pool CandidateHandle objects.

kevin: Also consider precomputing partial scores (warm_score * affinity_weight) in FastPath to bias warmed replicas cheaply. HeavyEvaluator can refine these with model-based latency estimates.

omar: How about batching for HeavyEvaluator? If many concurrent requests come in, we should coalesce evals for same tenant+route set.

nina: Good call. We'll have an eval-coalescer keyed by (policy_id, candidate_set_hash). Coalescer de-dups and fans out results. Add metric policy.eval.coalesced_requests.

alice: Migration: we should support an opt-in rollout: (1) runtime mode OFF = old resolver, (2) MIXED = FastPath returns same ordering as old resolver but exposes hooks, (3) ON = new flow including HeavyEvaluator. Rollout with data-plane feature-flag and canary.

david: Tests: deterministic tie-breaker unit test, evaluator-timeout integration test, coalescing stress test, adapter-shim regression test.

policy-bot: :eyes: Canary created: 3% traffic, regions=[us-west-2, eu-central-1], duration=36h.

kevin: Telemetry addition: span attributes decision.token, fastpath.latency_ms, evaluator.latency_ms, fallback_used (bool). Also record top-3 candidate ids in a compact tag for sampling.

omar: Security: ensure evaluator configs are validated from control-plane; don't let tenant-provided inputs affect tie_seed or determinism.

nina: Implementation notes I'll add to RFC: - CandidateHandle = {route_id, warm_score(float32), static_cost(float32), flags(bitmask)} - FastPath returns CandidateHandle[] + tie_seed(string) - HeavyEvaluator API: evaluate(candidates[], ctx) -> [{route_id, score(float64), reason_code}] with timeout semantics - Eval coalescer keyed by hash(candidates, policy_id) - Fallback: if evaluator fails/timeout, use FastPath ordering immediately and mark fallback_used=true.

alice: Keep PRs small: interface + unit tests first, then replace resolver internals.

david: One more: add an opt-in "prefer-warmed" knob per-tenant so we can A/B weight affinity vs cost.

nina: Will include that in policy schema. Thanks everyone 44b I'll draft RFC + example gRPC proto and post by EOD.

kevin: Lgtm. Ping infra when PR is up for canary config.

omar: Nice work, this should reduce cold-starts and keep hot path lean.

nina: Thanks!
